$comment: C11/C23 6.4.5 (D-CSUBSET-WIDE-HEX-OCTAL-ESCAPE-VALUE) fail-loud witness. THE CLAIM MOVED, IT WAS NOT DROPPED: this example used to pin the WHOLESALE refusal of u"\xC3\xA9", which is gone - that literal now assembles to the two units 0xC3 and 0xA9 (see wide_string_hex_escape_units, which asserts them by value). What remains fail-loud is an escape that OVERFLOWS the element, the one case where the references genuinely split: MEASURED 2026-09-02, each compiled and RUN, gcc 13.3.0 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 accept u"\x1FFFF" by TRUNCATING to 0xFFFF with a warning while clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51 REFUSE. A reference that only accepts by narrowing the value away is not one that WORKS, so the union over what works is a refusal. 0x1FFFF is a fine char32_t unit - U"\x1FFFF" compiles - so the bound is the ELEMENT WIDTH, not Unicode. The load-bearing pin is the CODE + a rejected compile at the literal position; the message names the width and the value.
